page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across compute and memory operations. The instance achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware flags such as AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI, contributing to strong performance in Passmark encryption and database operations. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient, placing in the top 25%, though large-block uncached read operations fall into the average tier.

This instance is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference. It demonstrates top-tier performance in prompt processing for small LLM models and strong performance in text generation for medium models. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its suitability for massive-scale deep learning training or high-I/O local database workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation and DDR5 memory architecture provide a stable, cost-efficient resource profile for enterprise applications requiring consistent general-purpose compute density.
